diagnosis.observed: After the 10:04:12 transfer re-INVITE, Initech PBX offered a new media port: 203.0.113.60:6200 (L16). We answered with 198.51.100.23:26002 (L18). At 10:05:00, fs-media-4 was still sending agent-leg RTP to 203.0.113.60:5000, the pre-transfer port. It was receiving from 203.0.113.60:6200, so agent-to-caller audio arrives and is forwarded, which matches the caller hearing the agent. The caller leg shows RTP in both directions with low loss and MOS 4.39. No line shows caller audio sent to port 6200.
diagnosis.suspected_cause: Guess: fs-media-4 did not update the agent-leg RTP destination after the transfer re-INVITE and kept sending to old port 5000 instead of 6200.
diagnosis.visibility_ends_at: fs-media-4 send and receive counters on the agent leg, at 10:05:00. We cannot see whether Initech's PBX received or played the packets sent to port 5000, or what happens inside the PBX after that. We have no capture on the Initech side.
diagnosis.next_check: Platform media engineer: on fs-media-4, check why the sofia re-INVITE handling for this call (Call-ID 91ac3e@198.51.100.10) left the RTP remote port at 5000. Look at the switch_rtp remote-address update and any media-bypass or re-INVITE settings. Then repeat a transfer test and confirm the stats show sending_to port 6200.

diagnosis.confidence: Fairly high. L21 shows a direct mismatch between the send port (5000) and the newest SDP port (6200), and the cause fits the one-way symptom. The re-INVITE log line (L19) mentions only the codec, so the reason the port was not updated is still a guess. There is no NAT problem: the PBX address is public and RTP is received from it.
